title: Hosted API: Stream-aware token slab pricing experiment
creator: Lina Moreno
description: Run a controlled experiment introducing a ‘stream-aware slab’ billing model that charges per-token with direction-weighted slabs and a short grace/crediting window for streaming sessions. Goal is to identify whether a slab approach reduces billing disputes for enterprise customers while keeping unit economics similar to the current per-token IO rates.
background: We currently meter ingress/egress tokens with asymmetric per-token rates and have multiple experiments around minimums and streaming floors. Enterprise customers have raised billing disputes around long-lived streaming sessions (chat assistants) where output tokens dominate costs but usage is bursty. The slab concept groups token consumption into directional slabs (e.g., first N output tokens priced at A, next M at B) and applies an adaptive grace that credits small tail bursts to reduce dispute noise.
goals: 1) Measure revenue delta vs current per-token baseline over representative customer workloads. 2) Reduce customer-reported billing disputes for streaming by >=40%. 3) Maintain gross margin on hosted API within +/-5% of baseline.
hypothesis: Introducing direction-weighted slabs with a stream-tail grace window will decrease billing disputes and improve perceived fairness for customers using assistant-style streaming while maintaining similar revenue and unit margin for hosted usage.
experiment_design: A/B test 12 weeks across a randomized sample of new and existing hosted API customers. Variant A = control (current asymmetric per-token rates). Variant B = stream-aware slab pricing: - Ingress tokens: flat per-token baseline unchanged. - Egress tokens: slabed pricing (0-1k tokens: rate R1; 1k-10k: rate R2; >10k: rate R3). - Streaming grace: last 3s of an idle streaming session are credited up to 250 tokens per session once per rolling 24h per org. Billing UI shows slab breakdown and grace credit line items.
sample_size: Target 400 orgs split 50/50 with stratification across: small (<$500/mo), mid ($500-5k/mo), large (>$5k/mo). Include 20 enterprise accounts in variant B as a flagged consult group for manual outreach.
success_criteria: 1) Billing dispute rate drops by >=40% in Variant B versus baseline. 2) Net revenue delta within -5% to +3% compared to baseline. 3) No degradation in latency/throughput metrics attributable to metering changes. 4) Positive qualitative feedback from at least 10 enterprise customers in consult group.
rollout_plan: Week 0: infra and billing modeling (ENG). Week 1-2: implement metering and billing UI changes in a behind-feature flag state. Week 3: internal smoke and finance reconciliation. Week 4-15: live A/B. Week 16: analyze and decide (rollback, iterate, adopt).
risk_mitigation: - Finance runbooks to reconcile slab invoices and automated alerts if revenue deviation >7%. - Fallback path to immediate revert to legacy metering via toggle. - Communicate to consult enterprise accounts with manual dispute SLA. - Legal review of contract language for enterprise customers before adopting slabs in agreements.
notes: We should separate slab buckets for long-running assistant sessions vs batch generation to avoid cross-subsidization.
Consider offering opt-in enterprise preview for big customers and include a one-off credit to offset change risk.
Metering changes must include detailed line-item breakdown; product analytics team to add new columns to billing exports.
decisions: Keep ingress per-token rate unchanged for the experiment to isolate egress slab effects
next_steps: Finance: build reconciliation queries and tolerances
Legal: draft contract addendum for slab preview
Sales: identify and recruit enterprise consult accounts (Marta)
